clue.text: Drilling site

parts.note: surface reading: a place where engineers bore for oil or water
setter's reading: the square where soldiers are drilled in marching

explanation.walkthrough: Drilling suggests boring holes, but soldiers are drilled too: the answer is a PARADE GROUND.
explanation.definitionFit: Military drill, marching practice for troops, takes place on an open square set aside for that purpose.

clue.text: Win over a hundred in a horse-race

indicators.note: being in something means placed inside it

parts.note: a plate is a race with a trophy as its prize
taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Someone collects a hundred pounds by winning at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: A plus C goes inside PLATE, a horse race run for a trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: To placate someone is to appease or pacify them, bringing them round to your side.

clue.text: Show resentment concerning level of noise

parts.note: re means about or concerning
the bel is a unit of sound intensity, ten decibels

explanation.surface: Someone complains about the noise from the neighbours.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebel is to resist authority, the action of someone who resents being controlled.

clue.text: Representatives get sealed orders

indicators.note: to order things is to arrange them, so these letters are put in a new arrangement

parts.note: all nine letters of these two words rearranged

explanation.surface: Envoys receive secret instructions in sealed envelopes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sealed orders' looks like a single phrase, but orders is a verb working on the words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Delegates are people sent to act or vote on behalf of others at a conference.

clue.text: The company go for the Scotch!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a band of people, a crew
second meaning: the Scots dialect verb for go

explanation.surface: Members of a firm head off for a whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Scotch' reads as whisky; here it means the Scots, whose word for go is GANG, as in Burns.
explanation.definitionFit: A gang is a group of associates, and in Scots dialect to gang is to walk or go.

clue.text: A musical proposal?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the orchestral piece opening an opera or show
second meaning: an opening approach or offer to begin talks

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a proposal of marriage set to music; the word is both an orchestral prelude and a first approach.
explanation.definitionFit: An overture is the opening instrumental piece of a work, and also an initial offer made to open negotiations.

clue.text: Being turned over, Edward is baptized

indicators.note: something turned over is flipped end to end, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: a man is a being, a living person
Ed is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A baby called Edward is rolled over during his christening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' looks like a verb but works as a noun, a living person; only that word is turned over, not Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: A child given a name at a christening has been baptized with it.

clue.text: Stretch a leg and note outcome

indicators.note: an outcome is what something works out as, so these letters come out in a new form

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An exercise instruction: stretch your leg and observe the result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stretch a leg' looks like one phrase; Stretch alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To elongate something is to make it longer, which is to stretch it out.

clue.text: A little girl's story about a donkey

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: A children's book tells of a girl and her donkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl's' looks possessive, but the 's is 'is' joining definition to wordplay. Lassie is the Scottish word for a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassie is the Scots and northern word for a young girl, a diminutive of lass.

clue.text: Sort of transport liable to ill usage

definitions.text: Sort of transport liable to ill usage

parts.note: surface reading: a vehicle likely to be mistreated or abused
setter's reading: a vehicle likely to be used by the ill

explanation.surface: A complaint that some kind of vehicle tends to be treated badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill usage' sounds like abuse, but read it as use by ill people: the AMBULANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An emergency vehicle carries sick and injured people to hospital, so its passengers are the ill.

clue.text: By no means all pay minimal tax in this country

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used, so the answer sits inside a longer run of letters

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of minimal and the start of tax

explanation.surface: A remark that in some country not everybody gets away with paying little tax.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'by no means all' as 'not everyone'; it really says the answer is only part of 'pay minimal tax'.
explanation.definitionFit: Malta is an island nation in the Mediterranean, so it is a country the clue can point to.

clue.text: Maintain a member in drink

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: ale is a type of beer, a drink
a limb is a member of the body

explanation.surface: Someone insists that a club member is drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests a club, but here it is a limb of the body; 'in drink' places that limb inside the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain something is to assert or claim it is true, which is what alleging means.

clue.text: Apprentices the boss sent on new course

indicators.note: setting off on a new course means changing direction, so these letters take a different order

parts.note: a boss is a raised knob or stud on a surface
the letters of sent rearranged

explanation.surface: Trainees are sent by their manager on a new training course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The boss' looks like the manager but is a boss in the sense of a decorative knob, a stud.
explanation.definitionFit: Apprentices are learners of a trade, and learners in general are students.

clue.text: Having caught it in the river, cause quite a stir

indicators.note: something that has caught another thing is holding it inside

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, a crossword favourite
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
taken as written

explanation.surface: An angler lands something in the river and causes a sensation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' does double duty: it supplies a letter and also signals that the river holds the rest. The Exe flows through Exeter in Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: To excite people is to arouse them, which amounts to causing a stir or commotion.

clue.text: A strike in town would be a disaster

indicators.note: being in something means placed inside it

parts.note: a large town is a city
taken as written
to lam is to thrash or strike

explanation.surface: A walkout by workers in the town would be catastrophic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests industrial action, but here it is a blow; lam is an old verb meaning to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: A calamity is an event causing great damage or distress, the same thing as a disaster.

clue.text: Get well-qualified group

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to complete a degree and gain a qualification
second meaning: to arrange or sort into grades

explanation.surface: Someone is told to earn good qualifications and join a team.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both finishing a university course and dividing things into a graded scale, as on a measuring jug.

clue.text: Fed-up with being a consumer — it's frustrating

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written, to be turned round
a consumer eats, so being one is eating

explanation.surface: Someone tired of consumerism finds it exasperating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed-up' reads as one word meaning weary; split, it is a word plus a direction telling you to read it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Defeating a plan means thwarting it, which is exactly what frustrating a plan means.

clue.text: Charges about a swimmer's sympathies

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: fees are charges for a service
the ling is a sea fish related to the cod

explanation.surface: Criminal charges against a swimmer have won public sympathy.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords a swimmer is often a fish; here it is the ling.
explanation.definitionFit: Feelings in the sense of fellow feeling or compassion are sympathies for someone.

clue.text: King has priest cast off and smacked

parts.note: R is short for Rex, Latin for king
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible
to shed is to cast off, like a skin

explanation.surface: A monarch defrocks a cleric and strikes him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smacked' looks like hitting, but means tasting with pleasure, as in smacking one's lips.
explanation.definitionFit: To smack your lips over food is to enjoy and savour it, which is relishing it.

clue.text: Remember to telephone again

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to bring back to mind
second meaning: to call a second time

explanation.surface: A reminder not to forget to ring someone back.
explanation.definitionFit: Recall means to recollect a memory, and read as re-call it means making another phone call.

clue.text: Pretend to have some influence

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to put on or feign, as with an accent
second meaning: to act upon or change something

explanation.surface: Someone merely makes out that they carry weight.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to feign a manner falsely and to produce a change in something.

clue.text: The coach for rough terrain

indicators.note: something rough is roughed up or disordered, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: all seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An off-road vehicle chosen for bumpy country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' suggests a bus for rough ground; it is a sports coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer prepares athletes or teams, the same job a sports coach does.

clue.text: Usually firm only after midsummer

indicators.note: after says the word before it is placed behind the word that follows, not ahead of it

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: mid points to the central part of the word it is attached to

parts.note: the two central letters of summer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A business that tends to be busy only once summer has peaked.
explanation.walkthrough: Midsummer is not a date here: with an even number of letters, the middle of summer is its central pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens commonly happens as a rule, ordinarily or in most cases.

clue.text: Noted play

parts.note: surface reading: a famous or celebrated drama
setter's reading: a drama set to musical notes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' means famous on the surface; read it as full of musical notes and the play is sung.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a dramatic work in which the story is told through singing and orchestral music.

clue.text: A shooting box

parts.note: surface reading: a lodge used by people out hunting game
setter's reading: a box that takes shots, i.e. photographs

explanation.walkthrough: A shooting box is a hunting lodge, but photographers shoot too, and the early CAMERA was literally a box.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographers speak of shooting pictures, and the device they use is a light-tight box with a lens.

clue.text: "All we have willed or hoped or dreamed of good shall —" (Browning)

definitions.text: "All we have willed or hoped or dreamed of good shall —"

parts.words: "All we have willed or hoped or dreamed of good shall —"
parts.note: a line from Robert Browning with its last word missing
the source: the poem Abt Vogler, about an organist improvising

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation: the line from Browning's Abt Vogler ends 'shall exist'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing verb completes the poet's promise that everything good that was wished for will truly be.

clue.text: Egghead sending up worker may cause an eruption

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a volcano rather than a noun

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of egg

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending a word up makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: the worker ant is a crossword staple

explanation.surface: An intellectual who mocks an employee might provoke an angry outburst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' reads as an intellectual; split it, the head of egg. ETNA is the volcano on Sicily.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is an active volcano in Sicily, a mountain that erupts lava from time to time.

clue.text: Trainee (male) has it in him to be flexible

indicators.note: having something in means holding it inside, so one piece sits within the others

parts.note: L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plates
taken as written
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A young male recruit is said to have the potential to be supple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It in him' reads like talent; really IT goes in between the trainee and the male to give LITHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe describes a body that bends easily and moves gracefully, so it is supple or flexible.

clue.text: Food diverted into Turin

indicators.note: something diverted is sent along a different route, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: all nine letters of these two words rearranged

explanation.surface: A cargo of provisions is rerouted to the Italian city of Turin.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutrition is nourishment, the food a body takes in to live and grow.

clue.text: But woman's hilarity is not occasioned by crime

parts.words: But woman's hilarity is not occasioned by crime
parts.note: surface reading: a woman does not find crime funny

parts.words: But woman's hilarity is not occasioned by
parts.note: setter's reading: the crime is the male, not female, version of laughter, split as a man's mirth

explanation.surface: A woman is said not to be amused by lawbreaking.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as MAN'S LAUGHTER: the hilarity belongs to a man, not a woman, and the whole is a killing without malice.
explanation.definitionFit: Manslaughter is the legal offence of unlawfully killing someone without intent to murder.
